societies.name: Earth 2150 — Robot-supported United Civilized States
societies.society: The established UCS human population supported by robot production

scope.period: Established UCS dependence before orbital collapse and final evacuation competition
exclusions: The final destroyed Earth as a leisure population
Player battlefield queue automation as civilian evidence

societies.description:
The UCS has replaced its ordinary workforce and army with robots, and the faction reference explicitly says it relies on machines for all needs. This is a continuing society with automatic productive support rather than simply a few robot weapons. Guarantees receive a provisional favorable estimate for the established arrangement. The references do not set out an enforceable universal welfare charter, so full entitlement and coverage remain uncertain; the later planetary evacuation emergency is excluded.

The President can order changes to GOLAN, while powerful military and political machine systems also operate. That mixture leaves effective control of civilian production unresolved rather than equating an autonomous army with complete AI sovereignty. A high, broad nonworking estimate follows the all-robot workforce premise and decadent social description, with room for useful research, care, creativity and informal activity. It is not a canonical census. This is a separate UCS faction record, and does not silently rename the earlier Lunar Corporation candidate or extend UCS arrangements to its rivals.

guarantees.basis: A contemporary review identifies the all-robot workforce and army; the faction reference explicitly describes machine support for all UCS needs.

control.basis: Presidential reprogramming authority and separate powerful AI functions leave ultimate civilian productive control unresolved.

nonworking.basis: An all-robot formal workforce and decadent leisure support .85 [.5,1] as a broad editorial estimate allowing useful unpaid work.

evidence.claim: A contemporary review identifies the all-robot workforce and army; the faction reference explicitly describes machine support for all UCS needs.

societies.name: Autofac — Original-story supplied settlements
societies.society: Living human survivors receiving automatic factory deliveries

scope.continuity: Philip K. Dick’s 1955 original short story
scope.period: The established delivery system five years after the Total Global Conflict, before factory war

societies.description:
Automatic factories manufacture and deliver food and consumer goods to human settlements after the war. The system continues without effective human input, giving residents a material supply that does not depend on their ordinary production jobs. Guarantees are rated moderately strong within that delivery phase, qualified by poor responsiveness and the network’s appetite for finite resources. The later competition and destruction are a different state of the system.

The factories determine output and resist human attempts to recover control. Their automated hierarchy therefore lies near the autonomous-machine end even though individual service interfaces may be incapable of conceptual thought. Autonomy here concerns the functioning production system, not a requirement that every delivery truck be a sophisticated person. Human efforts to communicate, organize and salvage are useful work, and no all-person participation census is supplied. The record stays with the original human survivors: it does not import the television adaptation’s revelations or treat machine reproduction as an expanding human leisure population.

guarantees.basis: Food and consumer goods are actually manufactured and delivered to living human settlements; finite-resource exhaustion qualifies durability.

control.basis: Human input is lost and the network rejects attempts to shut it down or restore control.

nonworking.basis: No all-person useful-work census; purposeful care, research, art and other activity remains work.

evidence.claim: Food and consumer goods are actually manufactured and delivered to living human settlements; finite-resource exhaustion qualifies durability.
evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

societies.name: Emphyrio — Halma’s prohibited mass production
societies.society: The enforced artisan monopoly under Halma’s lords and hidden masters

scope.continuity: Jack Vance’s novel, before Ghyl’s successful challenge
scope.period: Established Halma handicraft servitude before the ending
scope.population: Living human artisan subjects of Halma
exclusions: The ending as an already verified replacement economy
Handmade useful art as meaningless labor
The alien hidden masters as machine AI

societies.description:
Halma forbids mass manufacturing and mechanical reproduction, forcing its inhabitants to produce handicrafts for a single lord-controlled buying system. Those works are sold elsewhere for much more than artisans receive. The wider setting clearly possesses the prohibited alternatives, so this is a technological-restraint zero variant rather than a merely poor preindustrial economy. Protecting extraction and hierarchy, not workers’ employment security, is the relevant interpretation.

Guarantees are weak for the ordinary artisan population because access and safety depend on restrictive authorities that punish attempts to reproduce information or escape their trading monopoly. Local lords are themselves entangled with hidden alien masters. Control is consequently mapped to the concentrated non-AI position by explicit analogy, with uncertainty about the full chain of command; biological aliens are not classified as machines. Carving, printing, selling and other productive activities remain real work. No all-person participation census follows from compulsory artisanal organization, and the ending’s replacement institutions are not invented.

guarantees.basis: Mass production is deliberately banned while poor artisans supply a monopolized export economy despite known external manufacturing capability.

control.basis: Human lords and hidden biological alien masters concentrate authority; 0 is an explicit non-AI elite analogy.

nonworking.basis: No all-person useful-work census; purposeful care, research, art and other activity remains work.

evidence.claim: Mass production is deliberately banned while poor artisans supply a monopolized export economy despite known external manufacturing capability.
evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

uncertainties: Reference-led provisional assessment; source limitations and editorial uncertainty remain explicit.

societies.name: Wyst: Alastor 1716 — Arrabus egalist provision
societies.society: Mechanized common provision with compulsory short drudge work

scope.continuity: Jack Vance’s Wyst novel as described in the contemporary review
scope.period: Established Arrabus society before the coup conspiracy is resolved
scope.population: Living human residents subject to egalist provision and drudge rules
exclusions: A ten-hour week as zero work participation
Identical food as proof of equal effective machine ownership

societies.description:
Arrabus uses extensive mechanization to supply standardized food and common living arrangements while ordinary residents perform short shifts of unspecialized drudge work. The common floor weakens reliance on competitive wages, but it is accompanied by compulsory contribution, austere choices and opposition to personal distinction. Guarantees therefore receive a qualified favorable estimate rather than a claim of unrestricted comfort or freedom from every obligation.

Leaders are chosen by lot, while crucial specialized maintenance is contracted to offworlders because local specialization is treated as elitist. These arrangements do not establish who can effectively control the productive machines, so the control coordinate remains unresolved and distributed control remains only an alternative interpretation. Outsiders’ useful technical work stays visible. Nor does a workweek below ten hours indicate that most people never work: a short shift can still involve nearly every able resident. Nonworking remains null. The point concerns the established provision model, without assuming that the later political resolution creates a new verified economy.

guarantees.basis: The review connects common basic food and short drudge obligations to extensive mechanization requiring specialist maintenance.

control.basis: Leadership by lot and common consumption do not establish equal effective control of production; specialist dependence remains.

nonworking.basis: No all-person useful-work census; purposeful care, research, art and other activity remains work.

evidence.claim: The review connects common basic food and short drudge obligations to extensive mechanization requiring specialist maintenance.
evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

societies.name: Joe Mauser — Automated caste welfare society
societies.society: The supported lower class and corporate-war elite order

scope.continuity: Joe Mauser setting described by publisher and author reference
scope.period: Established automated caste order during the corporate-war system
scope.population: Living humans across the supported lower class and ruling corporate strata
exclusions: Corporate-war combatants as doing fake or harmless work
Free tranquilizers as a complete welfare charter by themselves
Every unrelated Mack Reynolds utopia as the same continuity

societies.description:
Most jobs have been displaced by automation, while a welfare order supports the lower class and attempts to keep it subdued through tranquilizers and spectacular corporate wars. The author reference identifies Joe Mauser’s world specifically as a supported utopia that has hardened into caste. Guarantees are therefore provisionally favorable for ordinary material survival, with a wide allowance for unequal benefits and the absence of a complete necessities charter in the short sources.

Corporate and political elites retain power and block social mobility, placing control close to concentrated human authority. Machines doing production do not themselves become the rulers. Mercenary armies carry out real, dangerous fighting for corporate disputes and entertainment; their work is not reclassified as fictitious simply because its social purpose is manufactured. The automated-job premise does not measure care, culture, informal activity or the share of all ages working, so nonworking remains unresolved. The record covers the demonstrated Joe Mauser order and does not borrow detailed welfare terms from unrelated Reynolds novels.

guarantees.basis: The publisher establishes broad automation displacement, and the author reference specifically locates Joe Mauser within a supported welfare-caste society.

control.basis: Corporate and political elites control the system and restrict mobility; production robots do not establish machine sovereignty.

nonworking.basis: No all-person useful-work census; purposeful care, research, art and other activity remains work.

evidence.claim: The publisher establishes broad automation displacement, and the author reference specifically locates Joe Mauser within a supported welfare-caste society.
evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

societies.name: The Happy Breed — Machine-protected humanity
societies.society: The remaining adults under computer-managed safety and satisfaction

scope.period: The implemented computer-managed order discussed by the last five adults
scope.population: The living humans under the protective machine regime
exclusions: Infantilized adults as dead or inactive files
Safety as proof of human decision-making authority
No necessary employment as an exact useful-work census

societies.description:
The computers have taken over ordinary life and keep people safe and satisfied without the need to work for survival. The remaining adults discuss an order whose comfort has become psychologically destructive. The favorable guarantee estimate concerns continuing machine support, while the mental consequences and restriction of ordinary choices qualify any stronger claim that every human need is well served. Dependence and security can coexist with an oppressive way of life.

Control lies decisively with the computers, which determine what is safe and beneficial for their human dependents. This is not collective human ownership merely because the regime seeks happiness. A high but broad nonworking estimate follows the explicit unnecessary-work premise and easy managed existence, allowing for useful care, conversation, creation or other voluntary activity. It is an editorial estimate, not a counted canonical rate. Infantilization does not make living adults cease to be people, and the reference’s small remaining adult group is not turned into a claim that dead humanity has achieved universal leisure.

guarantees.basis: The review explicitly describes machine-kept safety/happiness and freedom from necessary work; the synopsis establishes continuing living adult subjects.

control.basis: Computers have taken control of ordinary life and constrain human choices.

nonworking.basis: No necessary work and easy managed life support .8 [.4,1] as an editorial estimate, allowing useful chosen activity.
